data.long_meaning: Arabinda is a Sanskrit name derived from the Sanskrit word 'Arabh' which means 'to love'. The name is associated with the Hindu deity Krishna and symbolizes love, friendship, and peace. The name Arabinda carries the meaning “Love, Friendship, Peace” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Arabinda usually hope their child will grow to embody love, friendship, peace and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Arabinda stands out for its evident connection to the rich and diverse Hindu culture. Its origin from the Sanskrit language reflects a deep-rooted tradition and the value placed on the meaning behind personal names. In various Hindu communities, the name Arabinda is a symbol of love, companionship, and respect, as it reflects the love of Krishna towards his devotees and the depth of friendship amongst his followers. It embodies the essence of Hindu values and its significance remains strong within Indian and other Hindu cultures around the world.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Arabinda holds a profound spiritual significance for Hindus, as it evokes the unconditional love and compassion of Krishna. The name not only signifies the love between the deity and his followers, but also the reciprocal love and devotion between individuals. It serves as a powerful reminder of the importance of nurturing loving relationships and fostering peace and harmony in one's own life. Through the name Arabinda, Hindus engage with the spiritual aspects of their faith and culture, drawing inspiration and guidance for their personal growth and inner journey.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Arabinda: Radiant and Divine Love. Derived from the Sanskrit words 'ara' - radiant, and 'bindu' - drop or divine essence. Symbolizing the intense and divine love between Radha and Krishna in the realm of spiritual devotion.

historical_references.reference: Arabinda was a ruler of the kingdom of Kalinga in ancient India, who was converted to Buddhism by Ashoka the Great around 250 BCE.
historical_references.context: Ancient India, Buddhism spread under Ashoka the Great.

historical_references.reference: Arabinda Chatarjee, a prominent figure in the Indian independence movement, was a freedom fighter and a close associate of Subhas Chandra Bose. He was born in 1896 in Medinipur, Bengal Presidency, British India.
